newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia sets minimum prices for olive oil export.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia sets minimum prices for olive oil export.

text.p: Leading olive oil exporter Tunisia said on Friday it has set minimum prices for its exports of olive oil this season.

The Agriculture Ministry said the minimum price per tonne was set at 2,900 dinars ($3,016) for virgin olive oil (reference up to one degree acidity), 2,700 dinars ($2,808) for lampante virgin olive oil (three degree acidity), and 2,450 dinars ($2,548) for lampante olive oil.

The price for virgin olive oil was unchanged from its provisional level at the start of the season last November when the demand was at its highest. Prices for the two other references had not been set at the start of the season, agriculture officials told Reuters.
Tunisia forecasts that it will export up to 160,000 tonnes of olive oil for the 1996/1997 season.
This is a sharp rise compared to 1995/1996 when Tunisia exported only some 20,000 tonnes because of a two-year drought.
